[text-1] heading "Run tests"
[text-2] code "npx playwright test"
[text-3] "Tests run in parallel across all configured browsers, in headless mode by default. Each test gets a fresh browser context — full isolation with near-zero overhead."
[text-4] heading "Key capabilities"
[text-5] "Auto-wait and web-first assertions. No artificial timeouts. Playwright waits for elements to be actionable, and assertions automatically retry until conditions are met."
[text-6] "Locators. Find elements with resilient locators that mirror how users see the page:"
[text-7] code "page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })\npage.getByLabel('Email')\npage.getByPlaceholder('Search...')\npage.getByTestId('login-form')"
[text-8] "Test isolation. Each test runs in its own browser context — equivalent to a fresh browser profile. Save authentication state once and reuse it across tests:"
[text-9] code "// Save state after login\nawait page.context().storageState({ path: 'auth.json' });\n\n// Reuse in other tests\ntest.use({ storageState: 'auth.json' });"
[text-10] "Tracing. Capture execution traces, screenshots, and videos on failure. Inspect every action, DOM snapshot, network request, and console message in the Trace Viewer:"
[text-11] code "// playwright.config.ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  use: {\n    trace: 'on-first-retry',\n  },\n});"
[text-12] code "npx playwright show-trace trace.zip"
[text-13] "Parallelism. Tests run in parallel by default across all configured browsers."
[text-14] "Playwright CLI is a command-line interface for browser automation designed for coding agents. It's more token-efficient than MCP — commands avoid loading large tool schemas and accessibility trees into the model context."
[text-15] code "npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest"
[text-16] "Optionally install skills for richer agent integration:"
[text-17] code "playwright-cli install --skills"
[text-18] heading "Usage"
[text-19] "Point your coding agent at a task:"
[text-20] code "Test the \"add todo\" flow on https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc using playwright-cli.\nTake screenshots for all successful and failing scenarios."
[text-21] "Or run commands directly:"
[text-22] code "playwright-cli open https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc/ --headed\nplaywright-cli type \"Buy groceries\"\nplaywright-cli press Enter\nplaywright-cli screenshot"
[text-23] heading "Session monitoring"
[text-24] "Use playwright-cli show to open a visual dashboard with live screencast previews of all running browser sessions. Click any session to zoom in and take remote control."
[text-25] code "playwright-cli show"
[text-26] table row "Full CLI documentation | GitHub"
[text-27] heading "Playwright MCP"
[text-28] "The Playwright MCP server gives AI agents full browser control through the Model Context Protocol. Agents interact with pages using structured accessibility snapshots — no vision models or screenshots required."
[text-29] heading "Setup"
[text-30] "Add to your MCP client (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, etc.):"
[text-31] code "{\n  \"mcpServers\": {\n    \"playwright\": {\n      \"command\": \"npx\",\n      \"args\": [\"@playwright/mcp@latest\"]\n    }\n  }\n}"
[text-32] "One-click install for VS Code:"
[text-33] "For Claude Code:"
[text-34] code "claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest"
[text-35] heading "How it works"
[text-36] "Ask your AI assistant to interact with any web page:"
[text-37] code "Navigate to https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc and add a few todo items."
[text-38] "The agent sees the page as a structured accessibility tree:"
[text-39] code "- heading \"todos\" [level=1]\n- textbox \"What needs to be done?\" [ref=e5]\n- listitem:\n  - checkbox \"Toggle Todo\" [ref=e10]\n  - text: \"Buy groceries\""
[text-40] "It uses element refs like e5 and e10 to click, type, and interact — deterministically and without visual ambiguity. Tools cover navigation, form filling, screenshots, network mocking, storage management, and more."
[text-41] table row "Full MCP documentation | GitHub"
[text-42] heading "Playwright Library"
[text-43] "Use playwright as a library for browser automation scripts — web scraping, PDF generation, screenshot capture, and any workflow that needs programmatic browser control without a test runner."
[text-44] code "npm i playwright"
[text-45] heading "Examples"
[text-46] "Take a screenshot:"
[text-47] code "import { chromium } from 'playwright';\n\nconst browser = await chromium.launch();\nconst page = await browser.newPage();\nawait page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\nawait page.screenshot({ path: 'screenshot.png' });\nawait browser.close();"
[text-48] "Generate a PDF:"
[text-49] code "import { chromium } from 'playwright';\n\nconst browser = await chromium.launch();\nconst page = await browser.newPage();\nawait page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\nawait page.pdf({ path: 'page.pdf', format: 'A4' });\nawait browser.close();"
[text-50] "Emulate a mobile device:"
[text-51] code "import { chromium, devices } from 'playwright';\n\nconst browser = await chromium.launch();\nconst context = await browser.newContext(devices['iPhone 15']);\nconst page = await context.newPage();\nawait page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\nawait page.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png' });\nawait browser.clo"
[text-52] "Intercept network requests:"
[text-53] code "import { chromium } from 'playwright';\n\nconst browser = await chromium.launch();\nconst page = await browser.newPage();\nawait page.route('**/*.{png,jpg,jpeg}', route => route.abort());\nawait page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\nawait browser.close();"
[text-54] table row "Library documentation | API reference"
[text-55] heading "VS Code Extension"
[text-56] "The Playwright VS Code extension brings test running, debugging, and code generation directly into your editor."
[text-57] "Run and debug tests from the editor with a single click. Set breakpoints, inspect variables, and step through test execution with a live browser view."
[text-58] "Generate tests with CodeGen. Click \"Record new\" to open a browser — navigate and interact with your app while Playwright writes the test code for you."
[text-59] "Pick locators. Hover over any element in the browser to see the best available locator, then click to copy it to your clipboard."
[text-60] "Trace Viewer integration. Enable \"Show Trace Viewer\" in the sidebar to get a full execution trace after each test run — DOM snapshots, network requests, console logs, and screenshots at every step."
[text-61] table row "Install the extension | VS Code guide"

[text-63] table row " | Linux | macOS | Windows"
[text-64] table row "Chromium1 157.0.8103.6 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅"

options.scroll_down: scroll the page down a screen, when no block further down holds what the words ask for
options.back: go back to the previous page
options.press: press a key: enter, escape, space or an arrow key
options.read: read the page aloud or show its contents
options.clear: clear the text in the focused field
options.stop: stop what the browser is doing
options.none: not a command for this page: a remark, a question, a name, noise
options.play: music: find a song or video by the words and play it now, on YouTube or on this site as the words point — never the page's play button, which is a click
options.play_next: music: find a song by the words and play it after the one playing
options.queue: music: find a song by the words and add it to the end of the queue
options.say_time: appliance: say the time and date — 16:58, Friday 23 October
options.say_weather: appliance: say today's weather in the home city — words naming another place or a website are a search, not this — no forecast yet
options.say_playing: appliance: say the song playing — nothing playing
options.say_timer: appliance: say how long is left on the timer — no timer set

slot.instructions: Which words of the transcript are the thing the command carries verbatim: the address to open, the search terms, the song to play, the text to type, the key to press? Never the command word itself: "play X" carries X. A line with no command word, such as a question, carries itself: its search terms are the line as asked. Choose none when it carries none.

options.none: the command carries no words of its own

extent.instructions: Only when the action scrolls the page or a scrolling part of it: how far? Choose words when the words give a number of screens or pages; screen when they say nothing of how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as many screens as the number the words carry
options.little: a little: a third of a screen
options.screen: one screen, as Page Down does
options.end: all the way: to the bottom, or to the top going up

where.instructions: Where do the words point: at something on this page, at something on github.com that is not on this page, or somewhere else on the web?

options.page: on this page: one of the numbered refs
options.site: on github.com but not on this page: a page, a person, a post, a section of it
options.web: elsewhere: another website, or a search of the whole web

outcome.instructions: Is what the user asked for done? First: if a pop-up, sign-in prompt or challenge covers the page now, choose in_the_way; a cookie strip or other notice on the page that covers nothing is not in the way. Otherwise judge by their words and Done so far, not by the page alone: choose yes when the page shows what they asked to see (for a question, when Text in view states its answer), or Done so far shows the action they asked for has happened; not_yet when more steps are needed.

options.yes: done: the page shows it or its answer, or the action they asked for has happened
options.in_the_way: a pop-up or prompt covers the page now
options.not_yet: not done: more to do, nothing covering the page

progress.instructions: Did the last action in Done so far bring the page closer to what the user's words ask for? Judge by what it did and the page now: closer when it did part or all of what they asked, or opened the way to it; not closer when what changed is not what they asked for.

passage.instructions: Which block of Text in view states what the user asked to know, in the page's own words? Choose none when no block states it, or when the user asked for an action and nothing to be told.
